cso.prose: Over the two truth values, consider the claim that for every b there is some c differing from it. Now consider the same two quantifiers in the opposite order: that there is some c differing from every b.
cso.question: Does the statement with the quantifiers in the reversed order also hold?

answer.justification: The first claim holds by taking c to be the negation of b. The reversed claim asks for one c unequal to both truth values, and no such c exists.

constraints: forall b : Bool . exists c : Bool . c != b

distractors: assuming the two quantifier orders are interchangeable
reading the reversed statement as a rewording of the first
cso._note: reference_hml is deliberately empty. solve runs in reasoning mode: there is no reference encoding to withhold, because producing the encoding is part of the task. The withheld key is cso.answer and nothing else.

scripted_turns.generation:
The domain is finite, so both orders can be settled by exhaustion. For each b, choosing c as its negation works, so the first order holds. The reversed order demands a single c unequal to both truth values, and it has no witness. I name the reversed statement so its truth value can be read out, and require its negation.

```hml
module QuantifierScope

require forall b : Bool . exists c : Bool . c != b

def reversed_scope_holds := exists c : Bool . forall b : Bool . c != b

require not reversed_scope_holds
```
